A railway yard becomes a community garden

A place to grow

At the edge of the city, a former railway yard is becoming a new public garden. Local residents have spent the spring planting trees, building paths, and restoring an old greenhouse. The project shows what can happen when a neighborhood has space to experiment and enough time to listen.

The garden committee meets every Saturday morning. Volunteers bring tools and share ideas about water conservation and accessible routes. A local school has adopted several vegetable beds, giving students a place to study soil and insects throughout the year.

Funding comes from a combination of small donations and a public environmental grant. Organizers publish their expenses at the community center. They say their next priority is a covered meeting space where neighbors can gather even during the rainy season.

The site will open to visitors next month. Entry will remain free, and a rotating team of volunteers will look after the plants. The organizers hope other neighborhoods can learn from their work and adapt the design to their own streets and public spaces.
